events.title: The English capture David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross
events.description: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.
events.html: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.

events.title: The Second Battle of Kosovo begins between Hunyadi and Murad II
events.description: A Hungarian-led crusader army under the regent John Hunyadi, seeking to avenge the defeat at Varna, met the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad II on the Kosovo plain. After three days of fighting the Ottomans prevailed.
events.html: A Hungarian-led crusader army under the regent John Hunyadi, seeking to avenge the defeat at Varna, met the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad II on the Kosovo plain. After three days of fighting the Ottomans prevailed.

events.title: The University of Greifswald is founded
events.description: The University of Greifswald was founded in the Baltic town of Greifswald in Pomerania, with the support of Duke Wartislaw IX and the burgomaster Heinrich Rubenow. Under Swedish rule from 1648 to 1815 it was the oldest university of the Swedish realm.

events.title: Apraksin's Russian army defeats Armfeldt's Finnish army at Pälkäne
events.description: In the Great Northern War, a Russian army under Admiral Fyodor Apraksin defeated the defending Finnish army of the Swedish Empire under General Carl Gustaf Armfeldt at Pälkäne, though Armfeldt withdrew his army in good order.
events.html: In the Great Northern War, a Russian army under Admiral Fyodor Apraksin defeated the defending Finnish army of the Swedish Empire under General Carl Gustaf Armfeldt at Pälkäne, though Armfeldt withdrew his army in good order.

events.title: Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga
events.description: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.
events.html: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.

events.title: Riots against Aleppo's Christians begin, ending in a massacre
events.description: Muslim residents, largely from the eastern quarters of Aleppo, attacked Christian residents of the northern suburbs of Judayde and Salibeh in two days of rioting. Numerous people were killed, among them Peter VII Jarweh, the Syriac Catholic Patriarch.

events.title: Edison files his first motion picture caveat
events.description: Thomas Edison filed a patent caveat describing an 'optical phonograph' to record and reproduce moving images. The idea, developed largely by his assistant William Dickson, became the Kinetoscope.

events.title: The Queen opens Calder Hall nuclear power station
events.description: Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumberland, the world's first nuclear power station to supply electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale. It also produced plutonium for Britain's weapons programme.

events.title: Mother Teresa is named winner of the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced its Peace Prize for Mother Teresa, founder of the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, for her work among the poorest and dying.

song: A song by Rabindranath Tagore in praise of the land of Bengal that became the national anthem of Bangladesh in 1971.
